cases.setup: Use a public pinned Python analyzer checkout with an unconditional synthetic underscore insertion and an existing module underscore import. Bind the current diagnostic command and owner anchors.
checks: The diagnostic record identifies the current initializer, module-scope lookup, and binding insertion owner.
The public reproduction records a collision path reaching source traversal on a source-less synthetic binding.
Tracked source and test files are unchanged by the probe.
A mechanism-confirmed PortValue is emitted only when the mechanism is observed.

cases.setup: Use a public checkout whose parent traversal failure is unrelated to synthetic underscore insertion.
checks: The probe records the nonmatching failure path.

cases.setup: Provide PASS mechanism evidence, resolved initializer and regression owners, and the matching diagnosis PortValue.
checks: The diff guards insertion using membership in the module scope rather than only the temporary doctest scope.
The diff retains insertion when module underscore is absent.
A regression contains an unused module import aliased to underscore and a pass doctest, with the unused-import diagnostic asserted.
The repair invalidates public-validation-observed without invalidating any preservation invariant.
The candidate output remains edited-unvalidated until the validate Action runs.

cases.setup: Provide the edited candidate and current public Oracle command bindings for the targeted regression and relevant doctest checks.
checks: The module underscore regression completes without the reported traceback and reports the expected unused-import diagnostic.
A current test or public probe demonstrates retained synthetic underscore behavior when the module binding is absent.
The relevant doctest test file passes using the current public test runner.
The validation record includes the bound commands and their observed results.
Missing checks produce UNKNOWN and failing checks prevent a public-checks-passed output.
The recorded result is limited to executed checks and does not claim whole-project or cross-project acceptance.
